title: San Emilio Forest Dynamics Plot
alt: Slide 6: San Emilio Forest Dynamics Plot
transcript: San Emilio Forest Dynamics Plot ~16 ha plot: 680m x 240m rectangle All trees and lianas 3cm dbh measured and spatial position mapped Forest surveys completed in 1976, 1996, 2006, 2020 Plot initiated in 1976 by S.P. Hubbell and G.C. Stevens ~150 tree species in the plot

title: Why is this forest plot notable?
alt: Slide 7: Why is this forest plot notable?
transcript: Why is this forest plot notable? Tropical dry forest (seasonal drought, high interannual variation in rainfall) Long-term dynamics Disturbed It is in various stages of recovery from human disturbance A bellwether for the fate of more mesic tropical forests under climate change One of a relatively small number of dry forest plots Although only 1 census with ForestGeo protocol, 3 additional surveys with overlapping protocols provide 44 years of forest dynamics. An accurate reflection of an increasing large fraction of tropical forest

title: 1910s – 1920 Dan Janzen 11/17/2021…. “ [The plot] it was a banana plantation for the Casona occupants in 1920 (we do...
alt: Slide 23: 1910s – 1920 Dan Janzen 11/17/2021…. “ [The plot] it was a banana plantation for the Casona occupants in 1920 (we do...
transcript: 1910s – 1920 Dan Janzen 11/17/2021…. “ [The plot] it was a banana plantation for the Casona occupants in 1920 (we do not know when abandoned but sometime after that date). I learned that from Roberto Espinoza’s father, don Lupo Espinoza when I arrived in 1975 and was mystified by the pig ditches forming that enormous rectangle with the old ox-cart road along it northern boundary. Pig ditches were supposedly deep enough so that they served as fences to keep the domestic pigs (and peccaries?) out of the plantation. All of those large Enterolobium trees were planted by horses and cows after 1920 in the very open part of the plantation.” Evidence that fires from nearby pastures entered plot as late as the 1970s? Plot History – Disturbance The entire plot has experienced some sort of disturbance Spanish likely extracted large Mahogany trees within the plot

title: slopes did not
alt: Slide 34: slopes did not
transcript: slopes did not include the expectation for pure demographic stochasticity (i.e., a slope of 1) or from pure environmental variation (i.e., a slope of 2; Fig. 3). When considering only those species with 10 or more individuals during each census, we found that the power law functions were 2.32 (95% CI, 1.94–1.67) for 1976–1996, 1.90 (95% CI, 1.53–2.27) for 1996–2006, and 1.60 (95% CI, 1.20–2.00) for 1976 to 2006. Thus, when removing rare species, the confidence intervals on the slopes always included a slope expected given environmental variation Based on theory in Chisholm et al. 2014 Ecology Letters Slopes are greater than 1.0 Reject a model of pure demographic stochasticity driving the dynamics of this forest Fail to reject a model of pure environmental stochasticity when excluding rare species but reject it when using all species. Dynamics likely driven primarily by environmental drivers with some stochastic dynamics, most likely for rare species. Swenson et al. (2020) Ecological Monographs
